attempts.raw_response: This will help you estimate how long each visit will take and allow you to set a fair price for your services. Keep in mind that larger spaces or areas requiring deep cleaning will naturally demand more time and effort. You should also ask about specific expectations, such as whether they want certain rooms prioritized or particular tasks completed during each visit. Some clients may have pets, which could affect your cleaning routine or require additional time. Clarify whether trash needs to be taken to a curb or dumpster, and ask about any security procedures like alarm codes or key access. Finally, discuss payment terms and scheduling preferences before you begin. Having all these details settled upfront ensures both you and your client start the working relationship with clear expectations and avoids misunderstandings down the road.

pair.human_continuation: Usually, the amount of time it takes to clean is calculated by the size of the area and the amount of work you need to do. If you’re only doing a light cleaning, such as emptying trash and vacuuming, then it won’t take as much time as a deep clean. Your time may also depend on how many employees you have working and how efficient they are. Many estimate calculators are available online where you can plug in the information to determine how much time you’ll need to spend. Look at your notes and pictures of the area you’re cleaning and determine if you need any special cleaners. Make an itemized list of all the cleaners you’ll go through while cleaning and how often you’ll need to replenish them.
